security.title: Java: DoS Vulnerability in JSON-JAVA
security.description:
[CVE-2023-5072](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4jq9-2xhw-jpx7): Java: DoS Vulnerability in JSON-JAVA

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependencies:
  - org.json:json:20140107 (declared at build.gradle:17)

The parser bug can be used to circumvent a check that prevents a key in a JSON object from being another JSON object.

Recommended fix:
  - Upgrade org.json:json to 20231013 or later

security.title: json stack overflow vulnerability
security.description:
[CVE-2022-45688](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3vqj-43w4-2q58): json stack overflow vulnerability

Severity: HIGH

Affected dependencies:
  - org.json:json:20140107 (declared at build.gradle:17)

A stack overflow in the XML.toJSONObject component allows attackers to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) via crafted JSON or XML data.

security.title: Use of Obsolete Function
security.description: The code uses deprecated or obsolete functions, which suggests that the code has not been actively reviewed or maintained.

evidence.explanation: In KycConnectionFactory (line 10), Class.forName("com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc.SQLServerDriver") is used to manually register the JDBC driver. Since JDBC 4.0 (Java SE 6), drivers are auto-registered via the ServiceLoader mechanism, making this manual registration obsolete.

security.title: Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a resource after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the resource is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: In the KycConfig static initializer (lines 12-15), the InputStream is closed on line 15 but not inside a finally block. If PROPERTIES.load() throws an IOException, the stream will never be closed, resulting in a resource leak.

security.title: Missing Release of File Descriptor or Handle after Effective Lifetime
security.description: The product does not release a file descriptor or handle after its effective lifetime has ended, i.e., after the file descriptor/handle is no longer needed.

evidence.explanation: In the KycConfig static initializer (lines 12-15), the InputStream file handle is closed only if no exception occurs during PROPERTIES.load(). Because close() is not in a finally block, the file descriptor can be leaked if an exception is thrown.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Password
security.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: src/main/resources/kyc.properties (line 5) contains a hard-coded database password. This default password is shipped in the packaged artifact and exposes SQL Server credentials if DB_PASSWORD is not set.

security.title: Insufficient Logging
security.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: No logging framework is used anywhere in the codebase. KYC verification outcomes and SQL errors are never recorded in any audit log, making security incidents and compliance-relevant decisions unmonitorable.

security.title: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
security.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: src/main/resources/kyc.properties (lines 4-5) contains hard-coded database credentials: db.user=sa and a hard-coded password. These are bundled into the WAR artifact and used as fallback when DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD env vars are not set.
